tour.title: Project Architecture & Clean Architecture
tour.description: SocialNetwork is a full-stack social network platform built using ASP.NET Core Clean Architecture on the backend and React (Vite) on the frontend. The backend is partitioned into API, Application, Domain, and Infrastructure projects, while the frontend is a React SPA managing state via hooks and SignalR.

tour.title: Domain Model (The Core)
tour.description: The Domain layer represents the core of the Clean Architecture. It contains database entities like User.cs, Post.cs, Comment.cs, Follow.cs, and Message.cs. They do not depend on any outer layers.

tour.title: Database Context & Repositories
tour.description: The Infrastructure layer sets up Entity Framework DbContext (SocialNetworkDbContext.cs) and concrete repository implementations (UserRepository.cs, PostRepository.cs) for accessing the MySQL database.

tour.title: Application Logic Services
tour.description: The Application layer contains DTO definitions, interfaces, and implementation services (UserService.cs, PostService.cs, AuthService.cs) where the primary business workflows reside.

tour.title: API Endpoints & Controllers
tour.description: The API layer defines MVC Controllers (UsersController.cs, PostsController.cs) exposing RESTful JSON endpoints to the React application.

tour.title: Real-time SignalR Hubs
tour.description: Real-time features like chat messaging and instant notifications are managed using SignalR Hubs (ChatHub.cs, NotificationHub.cs) configured in the API project.

tour.title: Frontend Entrypoint & API clients
tour.description: On the frontend, App.jsx boots up the application. Under src/api/, Axios clients (axiosClient.js, postApi.js) call the ASP.NET Core backend endpoints.

tour.title: Real-time Frontend Connection
tour.description: SignalRContext.jsx provides a React context that initializes WebSockets connections to ChatHub and NotificationHub, exposing real-time messaging capabilities to components.

tour.title: Frontend UI Pages
tour.description: NewsFeedPage.jsx displays posts, and UserProfilePage.jsx renders users profiles. Hooks like usePosts.js manage the local component state and fetch data using the API clients.
